results.title: H100 price per hour, October 2026: 11 clouds compared · ClearCompute
results.author: Ronit Ahuja
highlights:
The short answer

On 5 October 2026, one H100 80GB SXM listed at $2.69 to $12.29 per GPU-hour on-demand across nine clouds, and the Vast.ai marketplace median was $1.80. Five specialist clouds charged between $3.20 and $4.50. The hyperscalers charged $6.88 (AWS), $11.06 (Google Cloud) and $12.29 (Azure), though a three-year commitment brings them down to between $2.97 and $5.40. For an inference server, four things matter as much as the rate: the smallest unit you can rent, egress, billing increments and how fast the price is moving.

...

We read each provider's public price list or pricing API on the same day. Where a provider only sells eight-GPU machines, we divided the machine's price by eight.

| Provider | What you rent | Per GPU-hour | Note |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Vast.ai | single GPUs from independent hosts | $1.80 | marketplace median; lowest $1.73 |
| RunPod Community Cloud | one GPU or more | $2.69 | |
| Hyperstack | one GPU or more | $3.20 | |
| RunPod Secure Cloud | one GPU or more | $3.49 | |
| Verda | 1, 2, 4 or 8 GPUs | $3.77 | $3.37 on 22 September |
| Lambda | 8-GPU instance | $3.99 | $4.29 for a single GPU |
| Nebius | one GPU or more | $4.50 | $3.85 until 1 October |
| CoreWeave | 8-GPU node | $6.16 | North America |
| AWS | p5.48xlarge (8 GPUs) or p5.4xlarge (1 GPU) | $6.88 | us-east-1 |
| Google Cloud | a3-highgpu-8g (8 GPUs) | $11.06 | us-central1 price table |
| Azure | ND96isr H100 v5 (8 GPUs) | $12.29 | East US |

H100 80GB SXM, on-demand list price per GPU-hour, 5 October 2026

...

## SXM, PCIe and NVL are different products#

"H100" covers three cards with different memory and bandwidth:

| H100 variant | Memory | Memory bandwidth | Lowest on-demand price we found |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| SXM | 80 GB | 3.35 TB/s | $2.69 (RunPod Community) |
| PCIe | 80 GB | 2.0 TB/s | $1.99 (RunPod Community) |
| NVL | 94 GB | 3.9 TB/s | $2.59 (RunPod Community) |

Each generated token requires reading the model's weights from memory, so for a single stream of text the speed limit is memory bandwidth rather than compute. NVIDIA's inference guide walks through why. Per unit of bandwidth, the SXM card is the better buy: $2.69 for 3.35 TB/s works out at $0.80 per TB/s-hour, against $1.00 for the PCIe card at $1.99.

...

## Prices rose this autumn#

- Nebius raised on-demand prices on 1 October: H100 by 17% ($3.85 to $4.50), H200 by 20% and B200 by 19%.
- AWS announced a 15% rise in EC2 Capacity Block prices from 7 October, taking a P5 H100 from $5.19 to $5.97 per GPU-hour.
- Verda's H100 went from $3.37 on 22 September to $3.77 on 5 October, up 12% in 13 days, according to the Wayback Machine's captures of its price page.

Any price survey goes stale within weeks, this one included. For today's number, live trackers such as gpufinder.dev, which polls 22 vendors every hour, and SkyPilot's GPU Compass are better sources. A survey is more useful for explaining what the number buys.

...

We loaded each provider's public price page or pricing API on 5 October 2026 and recorded on-demand list prices in US dollars for Linux, before tax and discounts. Where a provider sells only eight-GPU machines, we divided the machine's hourly price by eight. Google Cloud's accelerator price table doesn't print a region; the other tables on that page are for Iowa (us-central1). Azure prices come from Microsoft's public Retail Prices API. Vast.ai figures come from its public pricing feed at 15:30 UTC. Spot prices change minute by minute. Bandwidth-per-dollar figures are our arithmetic on NVIDIA's specifications. We did not benchmark these clouds for this post. Every source is listed below.

...

On 5 October 2026, on-demand list prices for one H100 80GB SXM ranged from $2.69 (RunPod Community Cloud) to $12.29 (Azure, East US) per GPU-hour. Five specialist GPU clouds charged between $3.20 and $4.50. AWS charged $6.88 and Google Cloud $11.06. The Vast.ai marketplace median was $1.80.

results.title: The same H100 hour cost $1.26 or $0.22 per million tokens — Summary & Key Points | TeckDeck.io
highlights:
- A rented H100 GPU can yield vastly different costs depending on request load. For one request, the cost is about $1.26 per million tokens, while processing eight requests drops it to about $0.22.
- Common pricing errors arise when costs are estimated solely on a single request’s speed, potentially overstating costs by nearly 5.7 times.
- Factors influencing real GPU costs include the number of requests run concurrently, idle time, and cold start times for the server.
- The measurements show not only the difference in cost efficiency based on load but also the importance of accurately measuring your specific server's performance.
- Understanding cost variability can help users better optimize their GPU usage and expenses.

results.title: GPU prices explained | Intelaris
results.author: Intelaris Research
highlights:
## Price per GPU-hour

Cloud providers quote GPU capacity per GPU and hour. A server with eight GPUs costs eight times the GPU-hour price per hour.

Storage, outbound data transfer and support are usually charged separately.

## Pricing models

On-demand: billed by the hour, no commitment. Reserved: fixed capacity for one or three years at a lower price per hour.

Spot: unused capacity at a discount that the provider can reclaim. Community and marketplace: capacity from third parties, with varying reliability.

...

A list price does not guarantee available capacity. AI Compute Prices shows availability where the source reports it.

## Spread in the market

For the H100, on-demand prices range from USD 2.65 EUR 2.38 CHF 2.20 to USD 14.38 EUR 12.92 CHF 11.93 per GPU-hour, with a median of USD 3.89 EUR 3.50 CHF 3.23, as of Nov 11, 2026.

Two other dated anchors come straight from providers. AWS announced price cuts of up to 45% for P5 (H100) On-Demand instances, effective 1 June 2025, consistent with the June 2025 step in the table (the index tier blends several hyperscalers, so it fell by less). And price moves are not one-way: in January 2026 AWS raised Capacity Block prices for its eight-GPU H200 instances (p5e.48xlarge and p5en.48xlarge) by about 15%, with steeper rises in some regions, as reported by DCD and The Register. Purchase prices for H100 boards and HGX systems were widely reported in the tens of thousands of dollars per GPU but were never published as list prices, so treat any single figure as anecdotal.
